newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN ON THE MARK AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN ON THE MARK AGAIN.

text.p: Germany's Gunda Niemann collected her second World Cup speed skating win in as many days with a victory in the women's 1,500 metres on Sunday.
Niemann, the reigning all-around World Cup and world champion, clocked a time of two minutes 3.75 seconds on the soft Davos ice to record her third win of the season.
A double-gold medallist at the 1992 Olympics, Niemann opened the weekend with a victory in the 3,000 metres on Saturday.
Svetlana Bazhanova of Russia was second in 2:04.24 and Germany's Claudia Pechstein, second behind Niemann in Saturday's race, returned to the podium crossing third in 2:04.46.
Dutch skaters dominated the men's 5,000 metres, claiming the top two places.
Bob de Jong, last year's junior world champion now in his first season on the World Cup circuit, picked up his second career win with a time of 6:51.21.
He was followed by compatriot Gianni Romme with 6:52.98 and Germany's Frank Dittrich in third with 6:54.63.
